To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the weak coupling constants and the Isgar‐Wise function are strongly affected by the infrared behavior of heavy quark propagatorto be more specific, by the parameter ν, and that the weak decay constant of B meson is suppressed by the mass difference E, and the Igar‐Wise function at maximum recoil is suppressed by the infrared parameter ν.

the infrared behavior of heavy quark propagating in the light quark field leads to the significant suppression of the Isgur-Wise form factor at maximum recoil and to the strong dependence of the weak decay constants on the mass difference between heavy quark mass and light quark mass.

in the model with the infrared behavior of heavy quark propagatorthe weak decay constants of B and B* mesons depend strongly on the parameter characterizing the infrared behaviour of the heavy quarks, whereas their dependence on the heavy quark mass difference is rather weak.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the heavy quark symmetry breaking due to the light quark confinement and the infrared behavior of heavy quark propagating in the light quark field.
the calculation of the weak coupling constants and the Isgar‐Wise formfactor in the model with a heavy quark propagating in a light‐quark field.
the heavy quark behavior of the weak coupling constants and the Isgar‐Wise function in the model with the heavy quarks propagators having the infrared singularities.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the heavy quark effective theory (HQET) is not applicable for the description of the weak coupling constants and the Isgar‐Wise formfactor in the heavy quarks limit.
the infrared parameter ν is the most important parameter of the model.
the heavy quark symmetry and the infrared behavior of heavy quark propagating in the light‐quark background are the two most important features of the model.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the infrared parameter ν is not a free parameter but is determined by the mass difference E and by the confinement parameter.

the heavy quark model with the infrared heavy quark behavior is able to describe the weak coupling constants and Isgur‐wise form factor with the same parameters, which is in contrast to the model without infrared behavior of the propagator, where the parameters for the coupling constants and the form factor are different.
the heavy quark symmetry is violated by the confinement of light quarks and by the infrared behavior of heavy quark propagating in the light‐like background field.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the infrared parameter ν is the key parameter for the description of heavy quark physics.
the heavy quark effective theory can be derived in a consistent way from a model with confined light (and heavy) quarks.
the infrared behavior of heavy quark propagating in the medium with confined light quark is important for understanding of the heavy quarks weak decays.
